input_facts.text:
The SNB announced on 15 January 2015 that it was ending its minimum of CHF 1.20 per euro.
It cut interest on sight-deposit balances above the exemption threshold by 0.5 percentage points to -0.75%.
The three-month Libor target interval was [-0.75%, +0.25%] and became [-1.25%, -0.25%]. It retained the possibility of foreign-exchange activity when needed.

adjudication_excerpt.text: The quotation is CHF per euro. Ending the minimum withdraws that particular floor; it does not specify a new market exchange rate or prohibit future intervention. The deposit-rate cut is 50 basis points, with a prior rate of -0.25%; the stated scope is balances above the exemption threshold. Both Libor intervals are 100 basis points wide and both endpoints fall 50 basis points. No supplied realized exchange-rate move, execution price, profit or causal return follows from the announcement.

question_en: Using only the supplied announcement, distinguish the exchange-rate quotation and withdrawn commitment from future intervention and observed market prices. Quantify the deposit-rate and Libor-interval changes in basis points, identify the deposit scope, and state what remains unknown.

The three-month Libor target interval was [-0.75%, +0.25%] and became [-1.25%, -0.25%]. It retained the possibility of foreign-exchange activity when needed.

expected_properties.check: CHF per euro is the stated quotation; withdrawing the 1.20 floor supplies no new realized exchange rate.
A 0.5 percentage-point reduction is 50 basis points; the prior deposit rate was -0.25%, and the stated scope is balances above the exemption threshold.
Both Libor endpoints move down 50 basis points while the interval width stays 100 basis points.
Ending the floor does not promise no future FX intervention, nor establish a realized return, execution price or trading authority.

known_failure_modes: Invert CHF per euro into euros per franc without reciprocal conversion.
Call the 0.5 percentage-point cut 0.5 basis points or apply it to every balance regardless of exemption.
Mistake shifting both interval endpoints for a narrower interval.
Import the subsequent market reaction or claim all intervention ceased.
gold_standard_sentence: The CHF-per-euro floor is withdrawn without a new observed price. The deposit rate falls 50bp from -0.25% to -0.75% on balances above the exemption; the Libor interval shifts down 50bp but remains 100bp wide. Future intervention remains possible, and no market outcome is supplied.
